question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4},{X}_{5}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ The log-likelihood function of the sample $6,\,8,\,2,\,3,\,5$ is

$$
l(\theta )=a\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +b\theta .
$$

What is the value of $a+b?$

current_example.problem: Suppose $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5$ is an I.I.D random sample with $X_i \sim \text{Exp}(\theta)$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta.$ Find the log-likelihood function of the sample $2, \, 4, \, 1, \, 3, \, 7.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x; \theta),$ where $\theta$ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n = 5$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x, \theta) = \theta e^{-\theta x}, \qquad x \geq 0.
$$

First, let's write down the log-density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡f(x,\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta {e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =n\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =2+4+1+3+7=17\end{aligned}
$$

and $n = 5.$ Therefore,  

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta \cdot 17 \\  & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -17\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
